messages:
sarah: FYI escalated from Support — AcmeCorp seeing long tail latency and 429s when Dedicated pool tries to scale. Customer says traffic spike at 09:22 caused requests to queue ~60-90s before success, some 429s. They reported repeatable repro with load test.

mike: Thanks. Can you paste the request IDs and any probe logs? Also did they hit minReplicas floor?

sarah: tl;dr: autoscaler started, but pods stayed in Pending/ContainerCreating for ~70s. Related logs: 
- req_id: rc_8a9f4c2d
- trace: trace-acme-2026-03-10
- observed metrics: scale.time_to_ready=72s, probe.retry_count=11, attach.latency.mean=58s

ops-bot: [alert] autoscaler: probe_rate_limit=429 for pool dedicated-acme-eu-west (09:22:11)

jon: Posting repro steps from customer: 
1) send 300 concurrent initial requests (seq length ~512) over 30s
2) they have minReplicas=2, maxReplicas=40, targetRPS=120
3) warm_pool enabled but warm nodes show Unready until image pull/attach finishes

jon: quick logs snippet: 
```
I0310 09:22:12.123 scale_manager.go:412] initiating scale-up: delta=8
I0310 09:22:13.981 kubelet.go:78] Pod dedicated-acme-7 pending: Pulling image
E0310 09:22:40.004 attach.go:210] blockAttach: attach latency 45.9s, backoff=2s
E0310 09:23:25.312 probe.go:132] probe failed: 429 throttled by registry
```

mike: Hmm registry throttling + attach latency + probe 429s. Could be noisy neighbor + hypervisor scheduling spikes on that host pool. Also seen cases where kernel-level IO stalls cause mounts to hang and kubelet retries.

rachel: On infra side: checked node telemetry for that timeframe — io.wait spiked on nodes in the pool, and host-level CPU steal rose to ~12%. We also observed cloud provider attach retries for volumes to same host group.

leo: Customer is on Dedicated with NVMe-backed local disks? If their warm pool uses host-affinity and many attaches go to same host group, noisy VMs can cause attach serialization. Suggest spreading warm nodes across AZ/host-classes.

sarah: Customer says they pinned warm pool to specific instance type for cost predictability. They can loosen affinity if we recommend.

mike: Short-term mitigations to reduce customer impact: 
- increase minReplicas to cover expected spike (set to 6) to avoid scaling combo at peak
- enable fallback routing to smaller quantized model variant for ~50% lower startup CPU and memory
- temporarily disable hostAffinity for warm pool so attaches distribute (risky but helps)

mike: Long-term actions: 
- add jitter to attach scheduling + spread strategy in warmpool controller
- add probe backoff/backpressure detection to fail fast and trigger alternate model fallback
- investigate kernel IO stalls and noisy tenant detection on hostpool metrics

jon: Can confirm setting minReplicas to 6 in a canary reduced observed queueing during a synthetic replay — requests success latency median dropped from 85s to 12s for that run.

rachel: Filed infra ticket INF-2026-128: "investigate host IO stalls + attach retries in dedicated-acme-eu-west" includes node profiles, dmesg, and provider attach traces.

sarah: Customer-facing note drafted: "We're investigating warm pool attach throttling causing delayed pod readiness. Immediate workaround: temporarily increase min replicas or enable model fallback. We'll coordinate a maintenance window to redistribute warm pool nodes" — customer OK with a temporary increase. :thumbsup:

mike: For triage — attaching commands we ran to capture metrics: 
```
# probe counts by pod
kubectl -n redwood get pods -l pool=dedicated-acme-eu-west -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.status.phase}\n{end}'

# attach retry traces
kubectl logs -n kube-system -l component=cloud-provider --since=1h | grep attach | tail -n 200
```

jon: Also adding a quick repro recipe for eng to simulate noisy-host: spin up a VM that continuously dd if=/dev/zero of=/tmp/testfile bs=1M & hammer with fio and run attach operations in parallel. That reproduced attach serialization in local env.

leo: I'll run a capacity sweep tomorrow to test warmpool distribution + set an autoscaler feature flag to prefer cross-host attaches.

mike: I'm going to implement a short-term rate-limit-aware probe hook: if probe returns 429 repeatedly (>5 within 60s) mark node as 'slow-attach' and trigger fallback routing. Will send PR with unit tests.

sarah: Great — please post PR link here and ETA. Customer escalation owner (me) will keep them updated.

mike: ETA EOD tomorrow for PR + E2E in staging. PR will include metrics emitted: autoscaler.attach.latency_bucket and autoscaler.probe.429_count.

rachel: INF ticket and a provider support case opened referencing attach request ids.

sarah: Thanks team. I'll update the customer and close the loop once infra confirms redistribution or we have PR + hotfix.

ops-bot: [note] incident_assigned -> sarah (support), ticket INF-2026-128 created

sarah: (closing) customer happy with temporary minReplica increase and fallback; will monitor and re-open if we see recurrence.
